{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past purchases as broad interest in related products or content, with insufficient attention to the user's current purpose.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Direct connections to recently chosen artists, recurring listening themes, and specific entertainment styles produce compelling choices.",
    "Practical accessories and tools appeal when they support an established activity or add useful capability to equipment already owned."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad category and brand connections repeatedly substitute for evidence of a specific need, producing unrelated project supplies and devices.",
    "Recommendations repeat functions already fulfilled by owned products without establishing a meaningful upgrade or replacement need.",
    "Broad entertainment similarities miss the particular mood, intensity, or musical qualities that make recent choices relevant."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, brand ecosystem, or general activity is treated as sufficient evidence of purchase intent.",
    "Multiple variants of the same product type receive strong representation even when the underlying need is unsupported."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent and repeated interests provide more specific intent than isolated historical purchases.",
    "Compatibility, existing ownership, and concrete incremental usefulness determine whether related hardware is worth choosing.",
    "Recognizable content connections support entertainment choices; unidentified items leave relevance uncertain rather than demonstrating dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top recommendations too often share a broad association with past behavior while lacking a concrete connection to the user's current task, setup, or desired experience.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "Track the proportion of top-ranked recommendations users would choose for an explicit connection to recent interests or an established practical need.",
    "Track top-ranked rejections attributed to unsupported activities, redundant functionality, incompatibility, or mood mismatch.",
    "Track repeated product variants whose underlying need users reject, and distinguish uncertain relevance from confirmed preference mismatch."
  ]
}
